title: AzureGate MedOps pilot intake - scratchbook
content:
Call notes (intro call) — AzureGate (09/18/2025)
Participants: Maya Chen (Redwood), Jonah Ruiz (Redwood), Dr. Leena Rao (AzureGate CTO), Marco Silvestri (AzureGate lead infra), Sandra Kim (product)

High level: AzureGate is a mid-stage telemedicine vendor focused on post-op remote monitoring. They want a small pilot (6–8 clinics) to add an LLM-assisted discharge Q&A and structured symptom triage. Must be HIPAA-covered and run inside their cloud region (gov-like constraints). Evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) vs. on-prem microbundle.

Primary constraints / requirements:
- PHI-in-scope: patient notes, vitals, images (x-rays/photos) may be uploaded. They need end-to-end encryption and KMS integration; HSM optional.
- Data residency: all inference and logs must remain in their Azure region (east-us-2). No cross-region fallback without explicit approval.
- Latency SLO: 95th perc < 250ms for short Q&A (single-turn, 150–200 token responses). For image-to-text + reasoning flows expect higher.
- Throughput: pilot ~120 concurrent sessions during peak; production could be ~2k concurrent.
- Auditability: per-request metadata, redaction trace, and long-term audit logs (365 days).
- Model control: want ability to pin model versions and test canary rollout of safety patches.

Core use cases discussed:
1) Discharge Q&A — patient asks about meds, restrictions, expected symptoms; model returns short structured answer + risk flagging for escalation.
2) Symptom triage — patient enters free text and attachments; system extracts structured symptoms and recommends next action (self-care, nurse call, ER).
3) Chart summarization for quick nurse review (batch job nightly, non-realtime but must be accurate).

Tech gotchas & notes from call:
- Attachments: images will vary in size; they want client-side resize for mobile before upload. Need to decide where OCR happens (client vs private deployment). Doing OCR in their VPC avoids PHI egress but may complicate our runtime (image->text preprocessor).
- Chunking: their notes are often terse but include templated headings. We should test chunk sizes 512–1024 tokens; embeddings for search should use sliding windows to avoid context loss.
- Embedding index: they prefer a vector DB in their VPC (managed) — ask about preferred vendor (CosmosDB + vector overlay? We suggested self-hosted Milvus/PGVector).
- Caching & prefix reuse: many dialogs reuse the same triage prompts — apply prefix caching to reduce per-token cost. Quick win for cost.
- Quantization: they are conservative about accuracy; suggest running 8-bit quant models for latency tests but have fallback to FP16 variants in Dedicated.
- Security: they want quarterly key rotation and ability to revoke logs on-demand. Need to map what Redwood Private exposes vs customer-managed KMS.
- Compliance: must supply a HIPAA BA agreement; legal pointed at enterprise onboarding.

Initial architecture sketch (brainstorm):
- Private control plane in Azure east-us-2 with customer-managed KMS (BYOK).
- Inference runtime in their VNet using Redwood Private package, with an internal ingress endpoint only accessible from clinic apps via a gateway.
- Preprocessing workers (OCR + image resizing) colocated; outputs pass through redaction module before indexing or logging.
- Embedding pipeline writes to customer-managed vector DB; retrieval served back to runtime with strict RBAC.

Prompting & safety thoughts:
- Use few-shot templates for triage with explicit hallucination guardrails ("If unsure, ask for clarification or escalate to nurse").
- Add a safety classifier (lightweight model) to detect hallucination/confidently-wrong answers and route to human triage when triggered.
- Redaction: run deterministic PII regexes and ML-based PII detection before sending to model. Keep redaction traces in audit log.

Suggested quick experiments for POC (1–2 weeks):
- 1) Offline: run 200 de-identified notes through summarization to compare model outputs (LlamaX-13B-256 vs Mistral-instruct) — measure accuracy and quality regressions.
- 2) Live: small in-VPC endpoint with 1 GPU, client-side OCR, prefix caching enabled — measure p95 latency on simulated mobile traffic.
- 3) Embeddings: build a proof-of-concept vector index (PGVector) and run retrieval-augmented Q&A with small prompt set.

Open questions for AzureGate (to clarify before proposal):
- Which vector DB do they prefer / are they open to Redbox-managed embedding index?
- Are images considered PHI by their legal (some classify photos as PHI; others do not)? Need explicit yes/no.
- SLAs: are they okay with a pilot-level non-SLA setup or need enterprise SLA upfront?
- Do they want redo of logs on delete requests? Scope of "right to be forgotten" across backups?

Next steps & action items (owner / due):
- Maya: draft a focused POC plan + cost estimate for Private (VPC) vs on-prem runbook (due 2025-09-25).
- Jonah: run offline summarization sweep on anonymized sample (50 notes) and report quality delta (due 2025-09-29).
- Priya: mockup onboarding checklist (BAA + KMS steps + network requirements) and share with legal (due 2025-09-24).
- Marco (AzureGate): send sample (anonymized) notes, a typical image sample set, and infra contact for VNet peering discussion (asked for by 2025-09-22).

Potential risks / blockers:
- If their legal requires on-prem only, deployment complexity goes up (air-gapped packaging).
- Vector DB vendor choice can add latency; need local benchmarking.
- If OCR is required server-side, the inference pipeline must expand to include GPU/CPU image steps — affects cost.

Quick follow-up agenda for next call (30m):
- Confirm PHI treatment of images, preferred vector DB, and pilot SLA expectations.
- Present two POC options (VPC vs on-prem) with rough TCO and timeline.
- Walk through onboarding checklist and network port list.

Notes to self: keep the early POC conservative (no heavy multimodal in week 1). Prioritize text triage and embedding-based retrieval. Emphasize audit/tracing features in proposal — that's the differentiator here.

End of scratchbook.
